title: nPOD
bodyHtml:
The Network for Pancreatic Organ donors with Diabetes (nPOD)

https://npod.org/

The Network for Pancreatic Organ donors with Diabetes (nPOD) seeks to answer the question of how and why type 1 diabetes (T1D) develops and to identify mechanisms for its prevention and reversal.

Data Types

Biosamples

Cryopreserved cells, snap frozen tissue vials with or without RNALater, DNA, RNA, paraffin or OCT slides, and tissues (pancreas, spleen, duodenum, peripancreatic lymph node, non-peripancreatic lymph node, thymus, serum, and whole blood). Available tissue preparations include fresh, flash-frozen tissue in vials, formalin-fixed and paraffin-embedded blocks, and fresh tissue blocks frozen in OCT media. Pancreas samples are available by region of pancreas (head, body, and tail).

Donor Information

Comprehensive human donor data, including demographics, clinical histories, body mass index, lab results, tissue quality, histopathology images, functional and immunophenotyping data, and measurements of autoantibodies (GAD, insulin, ZnT8 and IA-2), HbA1c, HLA, and C-peptide. Whole exome sequence data are available for many subjects.

Workflows and Standards

Following GLP practices, standardized procedures are available for sample preparation and processing, immune cell isolation, sample labeling, storing, and shipping; histology; immunopathology; functional assessment, DNA/RNA extraction; and cell cryopreservation and thawing.

Microscopy Imaging

Human donor-derived whole slide images of H&E and IHC stained tissue sections. Electron microscopy images are available for some donors who have T1D or positive autoantibodies without diabetes.

Omics

Genomics, Metabolomics, Proteomics, and Transcriptomics.

Data and Resources

Explore or submit nPOD datasets through the nPOD Data Portal or PanKbase. Explore nPOD imaging data through the nPOD Online Pathology Website.

Funding

nPOD is primarily supported by The Leona M. and Harry B. Helmsley Charitable Trust and Breakthrough T1D. Additional funding is provided by the NIH NIDDK to support autoantibody screening efforts for this program, in partnership with HIRN HPAP.

More About the Resource

The Network for Pancreatic Organ donors with Diabetes (nPOD) envisions a world without type 1 diabetes (T1D) and aims to identify mechanisms for its prevention and reversal. nPOD collaboratively procures and characterizes the pancreas and related tissues derived from human donors who have T1D or type 2 diabetes, positive islet autoantibodies, no diabetes, or various diabetes-related conditions. These donor tissues fuel research conducted by the nPOD consortium, which aims to understand the immunological, histological, viral, and metabolic signatures and mechanisms of T1D. Through the nPOD Data Portal, approved nPOD investigators, collaborators and their lab members can explore or submit data. Users can access and filter a list of donors and their associated publications, projects, and available samples. Through the nPOD Online Pathology Database, users can view whole-slide scanned images of H&E and IHC stained tissue sections for each nPOD donor. Users can access electron microscopy images of pancreatic samples from donors with T1D and autoantibody positive individuals without diabetes through Nanotomy Database. Raw images from both resources are also available for analysis upon request.

nPOD consortium working groups are currently researching the following major questions:

  • Defining the diversity of T1D
  • Defining the difference between T1D in adults versus children
  • Evaluating prohormone processing in the T1D pancreas
  • Defining the role of the exocrine pancreas in T1D development
  • Defining islet- and ß cell-specific targets
  • Developing translational therapeutic approaches for T1D

Some current nPOD research topics include:

  • Alpha cell physiology and dysfunction
  • Beta cell physiology and dysfunction
  • Beta cell development, differentiation, and regeneration
  • Core lab research
  • Exocrine pancreas
  • Immunology
  • Novel biomarkers
  • Novel technologies
  • Pathology
  • Type 1 Diabetes Etiology and Environment

More About the Team

The nPOD initiative is housed at the University of Florida College of Medicine and led by Executive Directors Dr. Mark Atkinson (University of Florida), Dr. Carmella Evans-Molina (Indiana University), and Dr. Alberto Pugliese (City of Hope).
